title.en: Phytoplankton: Oceanic Primary Productivity & Carbon Pumps
title.hi: पादप प्लवक (Phytoplankton): समुद्री प्राथमिक उत्पादकता एवं कार्बन सिंक

definition.en: Microscopic photosynthetic organisms drifting in aquatic photic zones, generating roughly 50% of the Earth's oxygen and serving as the foundational base of aquatic trophic pyramids.

content.en: Microscopic photosynthetic organisms drifting in aquatic photic zones, generating roughly 50% of the Earth's oxygen and serving as the foundational base of aquatic trophic pyramids.
content.hi: Microscopic photosynthetic organisms drifting in aquatic photic zones, generating roughly 50% of the Earth's oxygen and serving as the foundational base of aquatic trophic pyramids.

content.en:
• Major groups: Diatoms (silica shells/frustules), Dinoflagellates (flagellated, cause harmful algal blooms / red tides), Coccolithophores (calcium carbonate plates), and Cyanobacteria (Prochlorococcus, the most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth).
• Biological Carbon Pump: Photosynthetically fixed CO2 is transferred into deep ocean sediments when phytoplankton die and sink.
• Algal Blooms & Eutrophication: Excess agricultural runoff (Nitrogen, Phosphorus) causes rapid algal proliferation, resulting in hypoxic dead zones upon decomposition.

question.en: Which of the following marine organisms are primarily responsible for the phenomenon of 'Red Tides'?
question.hi: Which of the following marine organisms are primarily responsible for the phenomenon of 'Red Tides'?

explanation.en: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) or 'Red Tides' are primarily caused by rapid blooms of certain dinoflagellates producing potent neurotoxins (saxitoxin, brevetoxin) that cause paralytic shellfish poisoning and mass fish mortality.
